info.name: SKS Lotse Integration Tests
info.description:
Black-box HTTP integration tests for a real, locally running backend (ENVIRONMENT unset or 'development') - not the auto-generated API reference (see sks-lotse.postman_collection.json). Run with the Collection Runner, or externally via Newman:

    newman run postman/integration-tests.postman_collection.json -e postman/local.postman_environment.json

or scripts/run_integration_tests.sh, which also starts nothing for you - the backend must already be running (see backend/README or `uvicorn app.main:app --reload`).

Folder order matters: Auth Flow mints a token that Questions, Profile and Logout reuse, and Logout deliberately invalidates it, so Logout must run last among those. Account and Admin then log in as further throwaway users (each with its own token variable); Admin also reads the main test account and the account the Account folder deleted.

Cookies: 'Verify OTP' also sets the httpOnly access_token session cookie (ADR-0012), which get_current_user reads before any Authorization header - and Newman keeps a cookie jar across requests. So every request that authenticates via Bearer, or deliberately sends no credentials (the '... is rejected' auth guards), sets protocolProfileBehavior.disableCookies; without that, the jar would silently authenticate them. Only the requests with 'session cookie' in their name leave cookies on, to test the cookie path itself. Keep it that way when adding requests. Rate Limiting must run last overall (the 'Change email - per-user request cap' probe loop likewise exhausts that user's cap, but it belongs to a user deleted right after) - it deliberately exhausts the otp/request quota for this IP.

See docs/adr/0011-dev-only-otp-peek-endpoint-for-external-integration-tests.md for why this needs the /_dev-peek endpoint, and its limits (doesn't exercise the real Resend send path).

Not covered: RedirectSecondaryDomainsMiddleware (backend/tests/test_canonical_domain.py). It keys off the Host header, which both Postman and Newman silently drop/override rather than send as given (a restricted header, like a browser's fetch()) - there's no way to exercise it through this tool. Verify manually instead:
    curl -i -H 'Host: sks-lotse.com' {{baseUrl}}/health

MAINTENANCE: hand-written, not generated from the OpenAPI schema like sks-lotse.postman_collection.json is - nothing regenerates or checks this collection automatically. When auth/CORS/rate-limit/questions/security-header behavior changes, update the matching request and its pm.test assertions here by hand, in the same PR as the code change, the same way backend/tests/ gets updated alongside it.

SERVER REQUIREMENTS: besides ENVIRONMENT=development, (1) ADMIN_EMAILS must include the adminEmail variable (default integration-admin@example.com), or the Admin folder fails on its 'is an admin' assertion; (2) if ALLOWED_EMAILS is set it must include testEmail, profileEmail, profileNewEmail, adminEmail and victimEmail; (3) the question catalog should be seeded (alembic upgrade head) - against an empty catalog the catalog-content assertions degrade to shape checks; (4) run it against a freshly started server: the per-IP OTP quota (20/hour) and default quota (300 per 5 minutes) are in-process, and re-running within a minute hits the per-address OTP resend cooldown (stale dev-peek code).

COVERAGE GUARD: backend/tests/test_integration_collection.py fails when an /api/v1 route or /health has no request in this collection, when a request points at a route that no longer exists, or when a request neither disables cookies nor is a 'session cookie' request. Adding an endpoint therefore forces adding its requests here; and CI's 'integration-tests' job (backend-ci.yml) runs this whole collection against a real server.

item.name: Rate Limiting
OTP request burst (trips the per-IP quota)

exec: // Doesn't assume a fixed request count before the quota trips: the exact rule is
// 20 requests/hour per IP (app/main.py), but this run may not be the first hit
// against that path (the Auth Flow folder's own 'Request OTP' already used one),
// so detect the 202->429 transition instead of hardcoding where it happens.
pm.test('quota exceeded after ' + count + ' request(s): 429 Too Many Requests', function () {
pm.test('request ' + count + ' within quota: 202 Accepted', function () {
postman.setNextRequest('OTP request burst (trips the per-IP quota)');
pm.test('quota trips within ' + MAX_ATTEMPTS + ' requests', function () {
throw new Error('never got a 429 - is the 20/hour otp/request rule still ' + 'configured in app/main.py?');

item.description: Self-looping request (postman.setNextRequest) - reuses testEmail on every call, so only the very first ever triggers a real Resend send (the rest are skipped by the per-email resend cooldown - see OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS); eventually crosses the 20-requests/hour per-IP cap on /api/v1/auth/otp/request specifically (app/main.py's RateLimitMiddleware rules) and must come back 429. Run this folder last - it deliberately exhausts this IP's OTP-endpoint quota for the next hour.

Mirrors the *mechanism* proven in backend/tests/test_rate_limit.py, against the real configured rule instead of a synthetic one. The much larger general /api/v1 cap (300 req/300s) isn't separately drilled here - it would take 300 requests to trip for little extra signal.
